speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your current symptoms in detail, specifically focusing on the location and nature of your right knee pain and swelling, and how the episodes of pain with urination are manifesting.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and a history of inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I will request a Urinalysis and HLA-B27 genetic testing to confirm this diagnosis.
